evidence.intent_output: REL-PROXY-001: once handed to res.relay, the first of relayed-stream close() and the res.onAbort notification must close the backend socket. Core DefaultResponse.abort does not close the input while a copy runs, so the abort listener is the only thing that unblocks a relay copy waiting on a quiet backend; the suite does not pin that the abort notification ALONE closes the socket. Repro source and full output: .kiwi/analysis/kiwi-review-fix-loop-2026-11-18.naruserve.self-w16s10/repro/ReviewReproAbortClosesBackendTest.java, .kiwi/analysis/kiwi-review-fix-loop-2026-11-18.naruserve.self-w16s10/repro/ReviewReproAbortClosesBackendTest.output.txt

findings.title: No test proves the res.onAbort notification alone closes the backend socket while the relay copy is blocked
findings.description: driveRelayedEnd(CLOSE_AFTER_ABORT) only checks the socket after both abortListener.run() and relayed.close(); RelayedBodyStream.close() -> SocketBodyStream.close() closes the socket by itself, so the abort listener's socket close is never observed. ProxyLifetimeSocketTest AC-1 uses a DRIP backend with an RST client, so the relay's next write fails and the core's transfer closes the input itself. A regression where ProxyExchange.release (or the abort listener) stops closing the socket leaves the transfer thread and the backend connection blocked up to readTimeout (60 s) after the slot was already returned, so real backend connections exceed maxConcurrent, and every existing test still passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test (in ProxyExchangeTest or similar): relay from a backend that sends a head and a few bytes and then goes quiet, call res.abort(null) (or the captured abort listener) without closing the relayed stream, and assert the backend observes its connection closed within a short bound and the counter is 0. Also, in driveRelayedEnd CLOSE_AFTER_ABORT, assert backend.closedByProxy right after abortListener.run() and before relayed.close().
findings.real_call_path: TinyHttpd/any adapter reports a client disconnect (DefaultResponse.abortByExchange) or app code calls res.abort() while DefaultResponse.runTransfer is blocked in RelayedBodyStream.read on a backend that sends nothing -> abort listener -> ProxyExchange.release -> socket close is the only unblocker.

findings.title: A throwing Reservation.cancel() would replace the in-flight exception and skip closeQuietly(outgoing.body)
findings.description: forward's finally calls exchange.release() before closeQuietly(outgoing.body); a RuntimeException from cancel() still closes the socket and returns the slot (nested finally) but propagates out of the finally, masking the original 413/502/ProxyException and leaving the client body stream unclosed.
findings.suggested_fix: When the wave-18 watchdog lands, guard cancel() (catch RuntimeException) or close outgoing.body in its own finally.

clean_code.description: Options has a 15-argument constructor and 14 withX copy methods that each repeat the whole argument list; replacing maxConcurrent with limiter had to touch every one (17 of the 37 hunks). A mutable builder copy (copy(); field = v; return) would localize such changes.

withWatchdog is a test seam in the production class, and every option method silently resets the watchdog to NO_WATCHDOG through the 2-arg constructor, so p.withWatchdog(w).retries(0) drops w. The javadoc says to call it last, but the option methods could carry the watchdog through like the limiter.

forward handles the watchdog, connect, request write, response-head read, header copy, Location rewrite, relay lifetime and error mapping in one ~60-line method, and Proxy.java is over 1100 lines; the response-header phase could move to its own method.
NO_RESERVATION and RELEASED are two identical empty Reservation anonymous classes; RELEASED exists only as an identity sentinel, which a comment-free reader can mistake for duplication.

HoldingBackend (ProxyExchangeTest), HeldBackend (ProxyConcurrencyTest), LifetimeBackend (ProxyLifetimeSocketTest) and RawBackend (ProxyCheckOrderTest) are four raw-ServerSocket backends with overlapping accept loops, head readers and close detection; awaitCounterZero/awaitConnections polling helpers are also repeated.
